page.layout: One column of running text with a running head and page number at the top. Marginal notes stand in the left margin: "(b) Oft-Gothica." beside the section heading, and "Italiæ Regnū." beside the paragraph "Cum Romanorum". The page ends mid-word at the foot of the text block.

main_text.p: toto regno pulsi sunt, A. C. 1504.
main_text.head: Explicatio.
main_text.p: Primò quidem A. C. 1570. deinde 1647. Duce quodam piscatore, cui nomen Thomas Aniello sive contractè Mas Aniello. Cujus historia ut in recenti adhuc memoria, ita plena miraculorum.
main_text.head: OST-GOTHICA,
Canon.
main_text.p: Italiæ Regnū.Cum Romanorum Imperium in Romulo Momyllo Augustulo extinctū fuisset, Theodoricus Ostgotho-rum Rex, superato Odoacro Rege He-ru-

page.notes: The Gothic section heading "OST-GOTHICA," and the marginal "(b) Oft-Gothica." note contain a printer's dot after "G" in the margin; it is rendered as a plain hyphen. "Jtaliæ" is printed with a J and is transcribed as Italiæ (vowel I). The "ct" ligature in "affectarunt" and "contractè" is transcribed as ct. The word "Romulo Momyllo" is set tightly in print. The signature "A 6" is faint and uncertain. The paragraph continues on the next page after "He-ru-".
